title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation timeouts
author: Ava Thompson
description: Context: production traffic on dedicated pools showed increased p99 latency under mixed short+long workload patterns. The continuous-batcher scheduler was allowing long inference requests to monopolize the runnable slots while many short requests queued and occasionally timed out. Motivation: reduce tail latency for short requests without regressing overall throughput. This PR introduces tuning and fixes across the continuous-batcher scheduler and queueing logic to improve fairness and starvation prevention, and adds configurable timeouts and observability to validate behavior in canaries. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced a weighted queueing policy: requests are classified into latency tiers based on estimated request length (kv-cache hints + token estimate) and prioritized with a time-decayed fairness counter so older short requests get scheduled even when long requests are present. 2) Implemented starvation prevention by tracking per-tier wait-time and temporarily raising the effective priority of long-waiting tiers. 3) Added per-request soft scheduling timeout (default 500ms) that triggers fast-fail or fallback routing when the request cannot be scheduled within the soft window; these timeouts are configurable per-deployment. 4) Improved scheduler accounting to avoid head-of-line blocking by pre-allocating scheduling slots and using a small eager admission window for short requests. 5) Added metrics (queued_wait_seconds_bucket, scheduling_preemptions_total, request_timeouts_total, tier_priority_adjustments_total) and tracing spans to surface decision points. 6) Tests and benchmarks: new unit tests for fairness invariants, e2e canary harness with synthetic short+long mixes, and microbenchmarks showing p99 reduction for short requests with <=3% throughput impact for long-only workloads. Design notes: - The classification heuristic is conservative and only uses model sequence_length_hint + prompt length; no model introspection. - The fairness counter decays exponentially to avoid permanent priority inversion. - Soft timeouts are opt-in per route; defaults chosen after canary runs in staging. - We avoid preemption of actively running KV-cached requests; preemption only affects queued admissions. Backwards compatibility: behavior controlled by config flags in continuous_batcher.scheduler config; default behavior enabled for new Dedicated pools rolled out via canary. Related work: builds on prior continuous-batcher queueing improvements (see PRs: pr-41213, pr-45021) and ENG-3487. Checklist: - [x] Scheduler policy implementation - [x] Unit tests for fairness/timeouts - [x] Integration tests with canary harness - [x] Metrics and tracing added - [x] Docs and config examples updated - [x] Benchmarks run and attached in comments

review_comments: Rajesh Patel (reviewer): Can you explain why we chose exponential decay for the fairness counter instead of linear? Also please add a short note about the expected memory overhead per scheduler instance.

Ava Thompson (author): Exponential decay lets us bias recent traffic while allowing older waits to regain priority over time without tuning a long window; this avoids permanent high-priority for sporadic traffic. Memory overhead is small: two counters and a timestamp per active tier (~<256 bytes typical). Added note to docs.

Maya Rivera (reviewer): CI flaked on the e2e canary run — observed occasional nondeterministic failures when running with very small admission windows. Could we add a defensive assertion and a retry in the harness?
Ava Thompson (author): Added retry in the canary harness and tightened the admission window lower bound; reran canary and tests are stable.
Lucas Nguyen (approver): Verified perf results on staging canary: p50/p95 stable, p99 for short requests down ~180ms on 4-GPU pools. Approving to merge.
release_notes: continuous-batcher: improve scheduling fairness and add soft scheduling timeouts. Reduces p99 latency for short requests under mixed workloads. Config flags: continuous_batcher.scheduler.enable_fair_queueing (bool, default true), continuous_batcher.scheduler.soft_timeout_ms (int, default 500). Metrics: queued_wait_seconds_bucket, scheduling_preemptions_total, request_timeouts_total.
benchmarks_summary: Staging canary with 70% short (<=64 tokens) + 30% long (>=1024 tokens) workload on 4xA100 pool: short-request p99 reduced from 620ms -> 440ms, p95 stable. Overall throughput regression <=3% in long-only synthetic tests. Canary run ids: canary-2025-11-12-01, canary-2025-11-15-02.
notes: Rolled out to Dedicated pools via phased canary. Ops: monitor scheduling_preemptions_total and request_timeouts_total; rollback flag available at continuous_batcher.scheduler.enable_fair_queueing=false if regressions observed. Documented in docs/continuous-batcher.md
